blocks.source: Venite omnes pie mentes, Venite sinceri clientes, Franciscum Filii laudemus, Eique nunc honorem demus.
blocks.english: Come piously, all ye minds; come, sincere clients; sons, let us praise Francis, and now give him honour.

blocks.source: Quem humilitas exaltavit, Veraque sanctitas beavit, Qui in angeli altam sedem Lectus per luciferi caedem.
blocks.english:
Whom humility exalted
And true holiness made blessed,
Chosen for the angel’s lofty seat
Through Lucifer’s slaughter.
blocks.editorialNote: 10 October 2026: actual rendered PDF personally compared. Lectus is the regular perfect passive participle of lego, chosen, with an ordinary omitted copula in the relative clause; caedem remains slaughter, not an unprinted fall noun. The devotional claim is translated as printed without independent historical certification. Original prepared English/provenance archived; all Latin unchanged.
blocks.originalPreparedEnglish:

And true holiness made blessed,
Chosen for the angel’s lofty seat
Through Lucifer’s fall [printed Lectus is uncertain].

blocks.source: Deus, qui ad demonstrandam tuam potestatem servum tuum Franciscum, ob profundam ejusdem humilitatem in thronum luciferi collocasti, dejectum vero angelum ob superbiam humiliasti: concede propitius, ut ejusdem exemplo hic in terris semper humiles, in aeterna dein gloria exaltari mereamur. Per Christum Dominum nostrum. Amen.
blocks.english: O God, to manifest Thy power Thou didst place Thy servant Francis, because of his deep humility, upon Lucifer’s throne, but didst humble the fallen angel because of his pride. Mercifully grant that, always humble here on earth after his example, we may afterwards be worthy to be exalted in eternal glory. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

blocks.source: Deus, qui cor sinceri tui servi Francisci in tuo amore ita inflammasti, ut se votis obstrinxerit nulli quidquam amore tui petenti denegandi: fac ut pariter in nomine Christi postulantibus nihil denegemus. Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum Filium tuum, qui tecum vivit et regnat in saecula saeculorum. Amen.
blocks.english: O God, Thou didst so inflame the heart of Thy sincere servant Francis in Thy love that he bound himself by vows to deny nothing to anyone asking for love of Thee. Grant that we likewise may deny nothing to those who ask in Christ’s name. Through our Lord Jesus Christ Thy Son, who lives and reigns with Thee forever and ever. Amen.

blocks.source: Patris e domo ejectus, Dei filius adlectus, Patrem nostrum invocasti, Es expertus, quod optasti.
blocks.english:
Cast out of thy father’s house,
Chosen as a son of God,
Thou didst invoke our Father
And experience what thou desired.

blocks.source: Dulci eundem amplexu, Coluisti novo nexu; Inquiebas: Pater mi! Audiebas: Fili mi!
blocks.english:

Thou didst honor Him with a new bond;
Thou didst say, “My Father!”
Thou didst hear, “My son!”

blocks.source: Deus meus, et omnia, Caetera mundi somnia.

blocks.source: Deus, qui desertum a parente Franciscum, et teque sincere et filiali invocantem in patronum tuum praesidium recipere dignatus es: concede nobis filiis tuis, tibi filiali confidentia semper adhaerere, atque sub paterno tuo praesidio secure vivere. Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum Filium tuum, qui tecum vivit et regnat in saecula saeculorum. Amen.
blocks.english: O God, Thou didst deign to receive Francis, forsaken by his parent and [printed et teque sincere et filiali invocantem in patronum tuum praesidium: unresolved qualification/patron/protection construction]. Grant us, Thy children, always to cling to Thee with filial confidence and to live securely beneath Thy paternal protection. Through our Lord Jesus Christ Thy Son, who lives and reigns with Thee forever and ever. Amen.
blocks.editorialNote: 10 October 2026: actual rendered PDF personally compared. No unprinted paternum is supplied through fatherly protection. The actual patronum/praesidium wording remains unresolved. Original prepared English/provenance archived; all Latin unchanged.
blocks.originalPreparedEnglish: O God, Thou didst deign to receive Francis, forsaken by his parent and invoking Thee sincerely and as a son, into Thy fatherly protection [the printed clause is defective]. Grant us, Thy children, always to cling to Thee with filial confidence and to live securely beneath Thy paternal protection. Through our Lord Jesus Christ Thy Son, who lives and reigns with Thee forever and ever. Amen.

blocks.source: Te Deo plene dedicasti, Animam totam consecrasti, Postquam corpus cruciasti, Sanguineque sauciasti.
blocks.english:
Thou didst dedicate thyself fully to God,
Consecrating thy whole soul,
After afflicting thy body

blocks.source: Ordinis novi fundator Factus es, et propagator, E coelis qui mundo natus, Seraphicus appellatus.

blocks.source: Concede nobis Omnipotens ac Benigne Deus, per austeram vivendi normam et magnamque zelosi servi tui Francisci poenitentiam, auxilium ac gratiam, ut hic in terris nostrae conformiter vocationi in mortificatione corporis constanter nos exerceamus. Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum Filium tuum, qui tecum vivit et regnat in saecula saeculorum. Amen.
blocks.english: Almighty and kindly God, through the austere way of life and great penance of Thy zealous servant Francis, grant us help and grace to practice bodily mortification steadfastly here on earth according to our vocation. Through our Lord Jesus Christ Thy Son, who lives and reigns with Thee forever and ever. Amen.

blocks.source: Paupertati desponsatus, Et inopia dotatus, Hanc reginam nominasti, Factis tuis decorasti.

Thou didst call her queen

blocks.source: Dei opes solas veras, Praeter illas nugas meras, Agnovisti, et dixisti, Dives, pauper dum vixisti.

All else as mere trifles,

blocks.source: Deus, qui Sancto Francisco Seraphico pauperi quidem in hoc mundo, diviti vero in gratia tua thesaurum verae evangelicae paupertatis indicasti: tribue nobis veram heroicam spiritus paupertatem, ut cujus terrena omnia despicamus, et non aliam quam in coelis haereditatem devote suspiremus, atque glorioso obtineamus. Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum Filium tuum, qui tecum vivit et regnat in saecula saeculorum. Amen.
blocks.english: O God, to Saint Francis the Seraphic, poor indeed in this world but rich in Thy grace, Thou didst reveal the treasure of true evangelical poverty. Grant us true and heroic poverty of spirit, that [printed ut cujus terrena omnia despicamus: unresolved genitive reference concerning despising earthly things], devoutly long for no inheritance except in heaven, and obtain it [printed glorioso: unresolved case/reference]. Through our Lord Jesus Christ Thy Son, who lives and reigns with Thee forever and ever. Amen.
blocks.editorialNote: 10 October 2026: actual rendered PDF personally compared. Cujus and glorioso are complete forms but their references are not supplied through a repaired construction or unprinted adverb. Original prepared English/provenance archived; all Latin unchanged.
blocks.originalPreparedEnglish: O God, to Saint Francis the Seraphic, poor indeed in this world but rich in Thy grace, Thou didst reveal the treasure of true evangelical poverty. Grant us true and heroic poverty of spirit, that we may despise all earthly things [the printed cujus is irregular], devoutly long for no inheritance except in heaven, and obtain it gloriously [the printed glorioso is irregular]. Through our Lord Jesus Christ Thy Son, who lives and reigns with Thee forever and ever. Amen.

blocks.source: Orans noctes consumebas, Orto sole mox legebas, Sacra Patrum volumina, Delapsa coelo lumina.
blocks.english:
Thou didst spend nights in prayer;
At sunrise thou wouldst read
The sacred volumes of the Fathers,
Lights descended from heaven.

blocks.source: Deo laudes decantabas, Et canendo plus amabas; Exclamabas: O mi Deus! Et omnia totus meus.
blocks.english:
Thou didst sing praises to God,
And in singing love Him more;
Thou didst cry, “O my God!
And my all, wholly mine.”

blocks.source: En te cor meum diligit, Teque in patrem eligit.
blocks.english:
Behold, my heart loves Thee,
And chooses Thee as Father.

blocks.source: Deus, immensum mare omnium gratiarum et perfectionum, qui electo tuo servo Francisco omnia in omnibus fuisti, dum amore succensus exclamaret: Deus meus, et omnia! concede etiam servis tuis, ut in te unicum nostrum cordis lenimen reperiamus. Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum Filium tuum, qui tecum vivit et regnat in saecula saeculorum. Amen.
blocks.english: O God, immeasurable sea of all graces and perfections, Thou wast all in all to Thy chosen servant Francis when, aflame with love, he cried, “My God and my all!” Grant also to Thy servants that we may find in Thee the sole comfort of our hearts. Through our Lord Jesus Christ Thy Son, who lives and reigns with Thee forever and ever. Amen.

blocks.source: Seraphicae mentis ardor, Puritatis vitae candor, Deo semper eras gratus, Et ab angelis amatus.
blocks.english:
The ardor of thy seraphic mind,
The brightness of thy pure life:
Thou wast always pleasing to God
And beloved by angels.

blocks.source: Te calefasti parvum mundum, Abjecisti in profundum; Nosti quod sit caro coenum, Quo delectat, sit venenum.
blocks.english: Thou didst warm thyself, a little world; thou didst cast into the depths. Thou knowest that flesh is mire; [printed Quo delectat, sit venenum: unresolved connection concerning delight and poison].
blocks.editorialNote: 10 October 2026: actual rendered PDF personally compared. Te and parvum mundum can stand in accusative apposition with calefasti, the ordinary verb warm. The literal little-world imagery is retained without inserting a conventional renunciation narrative. Quo delectat sit venenum remains contextually unresolved; no unprinted quod substituted. Original prepared English/provenance archived; all Latin unchanged.
blocks.originalPreparedEnglish:
[The printed Te calefasti parvum mundum is unresolved.]
Thou didst cast into the depths;
Thou knewest that the flesh is mire,
And that in what it delights is poison [construction uncertain].

blocks.source: Mundum ergo debellasti, Felix victor triumphasti.
blocks.english:
Thus thou didst conquer the world,
And triumph as a happy victor.

blocks.english: Lord, through the merits and intercession of Thy servant Francis, most excellent in angelic purity, grant us undefiled purity of soul and body, that with a clean heart we may be worthy to behold the Immaculate Lamb forever. Through our Lord Jesus Christ Thy Son, who lives and reigns with Thee forever and ever. Amen.

blocks.source: Te sibi facit similem, Quem novit esse humilem.

blocks.source: Domine Jesu Christe, qui frigescente mundo ad inflammandum corda nostra tui amoris igne, in carne Beatissimi Patris Francisci passionis tuae sacra stigmata renovasti: concede propitius, ut ejus meritis et precibus crucem jugiter feramus, et dignos fructus poenitentiae faciamus. Qui vivis et regnas cum Deo Patre in unitate Spiritus Sancti Deus, per omnia saecula saeculorum. Amen.
blocks.english: Lord Jesus Christ, as the world grew cold, to inflame our hearts with the fire of Thy love Thou didst renew the sacred stigmata of Thy Passion in the flesh of the most blessed Father Francis. Mercifully grant that through his merits and prayers we may continually carry the cross and bring forth worthy fruits of penance. Thou livest and reignest with God the Father in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, forever and ever. Amen.

blocks.source: Qui odisti sublimia, Amasti vero vilia, Francisce hoc munus cape, Et ad te cor meum rape.
blocks.english:
Francis, thou who hated lofty things
And loved lowly things,
Receive this gift
And draw my heart to thee.

blocks.source: Fac ut ardeat cor meum, In amando verum Deum; Quo plus mundo sum abjectus, Hoc plus Deo sum adlectus.
blocks.english:
Make my heart burn
In loving the true God;
The more I am cast off by the world,
The more I am chosen by God.

blocks.source: Iste confessor Domini, relicto Orbe terrarum meruit beatos Exinde laetus penetrare portus Atrium coeli.
blocks.english:
This confessor of the Lord, leaving
The earthly world, was worthy
Thence joyfully to enter the blessed harbors
Of heaven’s courts.

blocks.source: Nam pius, prudens, humilis, pudicus, Nobilem duxit sine labe vitam, Et Dei mansit pietate plenus Semper amicus.
blocks.english:
For devout, prudent, humble, and chaste,
He led a noble, unblemished life;
And, filled with devotion, remained
Always God’s friend.

blocks.source: Inter electos sine fine gaudet, Osculum sanctae recipitque pacis, Sortis aeternae meruitque salutis Exsultat in aevum.
blocks.english: Among the elect he rejoices without end, and receives the kiss of holy peace, and has merited the kiss of the eternal lot of salvation; he exults for ever.
blocks.editorialNote: 10 October 2026: actual rendered PDF personally compared. Meruit is a regular perfect finite verb, has merited, sharing the earlier accusative Osculum as object. Sortis aeternae salutis remains genitive qualifying that kiss; no unprinted accusative sortem or adjective worthy supplied. This literal poetic metaphor does not need a Latin repair. Original prepared English/provenance archived; all Latin unchanged.
blocks.originalPreparedEnglish:
Among the elect he rejoices without end,
Receives the kiss of holy peace,
And, worthy of the lot of eternal salvation,
Exults forever [printed syntax irregular].

blocks.source: Propter ingentis meriti valorem, Hactenus multi potitiuntur aegri Viribus morbi domitis, salute Suppeditata.
blocks.english:
By the power of his great merit,
Many sick have since [printed potitiuntur: unresolved verb],
The forces of disease subdued,
Health supplied.
blocks.editorialNote: 10 October 2026: actual rendered PDF personally compared. The verb potitiuntur remains explicit at its location; received is not substituted as a conjectural finite verb. Original prepared English/provenance archived; all Latin unchanged.
blocks.originalPreparedEnglish:
By the power of his great merit,
Many sick have since received,
The forces of disease subdued,
Health supplied [potitiuntur is irregular].

blocks.source: Reddit hinc illi chorus iste noster Omne per vitae viridantis aevum Maximas laudes celebresque palmas Exhilaratus.
blocks.english:
Therefore this choir of ours, gladdened,
Throughout the whole span of flourishing life,
Renders him greatest praises
And celebrated palms.

blocks.source: Rector immensi Dominusque coeli, Spiritus Sanctus, Pater atque Natus, Trinus ac unus tibi sint honores, Gloria, virtus.
blocks.english:
Ruler and Lord of boundless heaven,
Holy Spirit, Father, and Son,
Three and One, to Thee be honors,
Glory and power.

blocks.source: Deus, qui Ecclesiam tuam Beati Francisci meritis foetu novae prolis amplificas: tribue nobis ex ejus imitatione terrena despicere, et coelestium donorum semper participatione gaudere. Per Dominum nostrum Jesum Christum Filium tuum, qui tecum vivit et regnat in saecula saeculorum. Amen.
blocks.english: O God, through the merits of blessed Francis Thou dost enlarge Thy Church by the birth of new offspring. Grant us, in imitation of him, to despise earthly things and always rejoice in sharing heavenly gifts. Through our Lord Jesus Christ Thy Son, who lives and reigns with Thee forever and ever. Amen.

blocks.source: Patronum eligendi
blocks.english: For choosing a patron
blocks.editorialNote: The printed passage was visually compared with this office’s source pages; its abbreviated form is retained.

blocks.source: Me lecte Patrone S. Francisce Seraphice, protector omnium te invocantium, praeprimis clientum tuorum, Ecce ego N. N. eligo te in praesentia Sanctissimae Trinitatis, S. Mariae, S. Josephi, totiusque coelestis curiae in dilectissimum meum patrem, patronum, et advocatum. Rogoque, impetra mihi a Deo gratiam, ut constanter in virtutibus ad imitationem tuam maxime in profundissima humilitate, abnegatione propria in serventi erga Deum amore me exerceam, et per intercessionem tuam felicem vitae finem obtineam.
blocks.english: My chosen patron, Saint Francis the Seraphic, protector of all who invoke thee, especially thy clients: behold, I, N. N., choose thee in the presence of the most holy Trinity, Saint Mary, Saint Joseph, and the entire heavenly court as my most beloved father, patron, and advocate. I ask thee to obtain for me from God grace to practice virtues steadfastly in imitation of thee, especially deepest humility, self-denial, and [printed serventi: unresolved qualifier] love toward God, and through thy intercession to obtain a happy end of life.
blocks.editorialNote: 10 October 2026: actual rendered PDF personally compared. Actual serventi is not silently replaced by ferventi through fervent love. Original prepared English/provenance archived; all Latin unchanged.
blocks.originalPreparedEnglish: My chosen patron, Saint Francis the Seraphic, protector of all who invoke thee, especially thy clients: behold, I, N. N., choose thee in the presence of the most holy Trinity, Saint Mary, Saint Joseph, and the entire heavenly court as my most beloved father, patron, and advocate. I ask thee to obtain for me from God grace to practice virtues steadfastly in imitation of thee, especially deepest humility, self-denial, and fervent love toward God [serventi is an irregular printed form], and through thy intercession to obtain a happy end of life.

blocks.source: Propono mihi etiam te nunquam derelicturum, neque contra te aliquid dicturum aut facturum neque permittendum: ut a meis subditis contra te unquam aliquid agatur.
blocks.english: I also resolve never to forsake thee, nor say or do anything against thee, nor permit anything against thee ever to be done by those subject to me.

blocks.source: Obsecro te igitur, suscipe me in servum perpetuum, et commenda me divinae misericordiae, sanguineisque vulneribus Crucifixi Jesu. Adjuva me etiam amantissime pater non solum omni momento vitae meae, sed et quam maxime in articulo mortis.
blocks.english: Therefore I beseech thee, receive me as thy perpetual servant and commend me to divine mercy and to the bloody wounds of Jesus crucified. Help me also, most loving father, not only at every moment of my life but especially at the hour of death.

blocks.source: Ah! tunc ne deseras me, o Sancte Pater Francisce, verum protege tunc anxium sub paterno tuo praesidio, et quidquid infirmitas mea non poterit, id mihi impetra per tuam potentem intercessionem: ut omnis sciat ac agnoscat, quam vere tuorum clientum recordaris.
blocks.english: Ah, then do not forsake me, holy Father Francis, but protect me in my distress beneath thy paternal shelter. Whatever my weakness cannot do, obtain it for me by thy powerful intercession, that everyone may know and acknowledge how truly thou rememberest thy clients.

sections.title: Devota Oratio ad S. Patrem Franciscum
sections.sourceHeading: Devota Oratio ad S. Patrem Franciscum

blocks.source: Seraphicum
blocks.english: Seraphic
blocks.editorialNote: The printed passage was visually compared with this office’s source pages; its abbreviated form is retained.

blocks.source: Beatissime ac Seraphice Pater Francisce, vere imitator Crucifixi Jesu, qui te prae omnibus aliis sanctis singulari amoris honorisque gratia ornavit, tuam enim animam lumine amoris replevit, atque in corpore sacratissima vulnera sua renovavit: per eundem amorem benignissimi Salvatoris nostri Jesu Christi supplices rogamus, velis semper apud Deum esse adjutor noster, protector, pater, et advocatus.
blocks.english: Most blessed and seraphic Father Francis, true imitator of Jesus crucified, who adorned thee above all other saints with a special grace of love and honor: He filled thy soul with the light of love and renewed His most sacred wounds in thy body. Through this same love of our most kindly Savior Jesus Christ we humbly ask thee always to be our helper, protector, father, and advocate before God.

blocks.source: O coelestis Seraphim, humillime Francisce, ora pro nobis, ut passio et mors acerbissima Domini nostri Jesu Christi non sit nobis reatus ad poenam, sed intercessio salutaris ad vitam aeternam.
blocks.english: O heavenly seraph, most humble Francis, pray for us that the Passion and most bitter death of our Lord Jesus Christ may not be for us guilt unto punishment, but saving intercession unto eternal life.

blocks.source: Benignissime Seraphim Sancte Pater Francisce! nos miseri peccatores fugimus ad te, et coram te genua flectimus, nos totos tibi tradimus, commonefque magni illius amoris quem erga peccatores miseros habuisti, ita ut a Christo nihil aliud quam peccatorum alienorum remissionem petieris, vi cujus innumerabiles animae aeterna beatitudine perfruuntur.
blocks.english: Most kindly seraph, holy Father Francis, we miserable sinners flee to thee and bend our knees before thee, giving ourselves wholly to thee. [printed commonefque: unresolved verb] of that great love thou hadst for miserable sinners, so that thou didst ask Christ for nothing other than the forgiveness of others’ sins, through which countless souls enjoy eternal blessedness.
blocks.editorialNote: 10 October 2026: actual rendered PDF personally compared. Printed commonefque remains explicitly unresolved rather than an invented remember command. Original prepared English/provenance archived; all Latin unchanged.
blocks.originalPreparedEnglish: Most kindly seraph, holy Father Francis, we miserable sinners flee to thee and bend our knees before thee, giving ourselves wholly to thee. Remember that great love thou hadst for miserable sinners [the printed commonefque is defective], so that thou didst ask Christ for nothing other than the forgiveness of others’ sins, through which countless souls enjoy eternal blessedness.

blocks.source: Misericordissime Seraphim Sancte Pater Francisce! miserere omnium morientium, et ora pro illis ut ante obitum plenariam indulgentiam omnium suorum peccatorum obtinere, et aeterna gaudia consequi mereantur.
blocks.english: Most merciful seraph, holy Father Francis, have mercy upon all the dying and pray for them, that before death they may obtain the plenary remission of all their sins and be worthy to attain eternal joys.

blocks.source: Zelotissime Seraphim Sancte Pater Francisce! ora pro omnibus in purgatorio animabus existentibus, ut aspectu Dei quam primum frui queant.
blocks.english: Most zealous seraph, holy Father Francis, pray for all souls in purgatory, that they may enjoy the sight of God as soon as possible.

blocks.source: Beatissime Seraphim Sancte Pater Francisce! non admitte, ut nos miseri peccatores in peccatis nostris moriamur, verum intercede pro nobis apud Deum, et impetra indulgentiam plenariam omnium nostrorum peccatorum: ut a poena liberati ex hac misera vita transitum faciamus ad vitam aeternam, ubi inter choros angelorum collocati tecum, et cum illis hunc gaudiosum Deo accinamus applausum: Sanctus, Sanctus, Sanctus Dominus Deus Sabaoth. Amen.
blocks.english: Most blessed seraph, holy Father Francis, do not permit us miserable sinners to die in our sins, but intercede for us with God and obtain the plenary remission of all our sins. Freed from punishment, may we pass from this miserable life to eternal life, where, placed among the choirs of angels, with thee and with them we may sing this joyful acclamation to God: Holy, Holy, Holy, Lord God of hosts. Amen.

blocks.source: Devotio brevis de quinque Vulneribus Christi Quae dilecto servo tuo Francisco impressisti, per quinque dies Veneris peragenda; quibus diebus sacra confessio et communio requiritur, additis (expansis manibus) septem Pater noster et septem Ave.
blocks.english: A short devotion to the five wounds of Christ which Thou didst imprint upon Thy beloved servant Francis, to be performed over five Fridays. On these days sacramental confession and Communion are required, adding, with outstretched hands, seven Our Fathers and seven Hail Marys.

blocks.source: Domine Jesu Christe! per vulnus sacratissimum manus dexterae, quod sincero servo tuo Francisco in signum singularis gratiae voluisti imprimere: rogo te, colloca me tandem etiam ad dexteram tuam. Amen.
blocks.english: Lord Jesus Christ, through the most sacred wound of Thy right hand, which Thou didst will to imprint upon Thy sincere servant Francis as a sign of special grace: I ask Thee to place me at last also at Thy right hand. Amen.

blocks.source: Pater noster, et Ave Maria, etc.
blocks.english: Our Father and Hail Mary, etc.
blocks.editorialNote: The printed passage was visually compared with this office’s source pages; its abbreviated form is retained.

blocks.source: Domine Jesu Christe! per sacratissimum vulnus manus sinistrae, quod sincero tuo servo Francisco in signum singularis gratiae voluisti imprimere: quaeso, tribue mihi verum filialem timorem, et gratiam superandi omnes tentationes. Amen.
blocks.english: Lord Jesus Christ, through the most sacred wound of Thy left hand, which Thou didst will to imprint upon Thy sincere servant Francis as a sign of special grace: I beseech Thee, grant me true filial fear and grace to overcome all temptations. Amen.

blocks.source: Pater noster, et Ave Maria, etc.
blocks.english: Our Father and Hail Mary, etc.

blocks.source: Domine Jesu Christe! per sacratum vulnus dexteri pedis, quod sincero tuo servo Francisco in signum singularis gratiae voluisti imprimere: rogo te, concede mihi verum et perfectum dolorem de peccatis meis, et duce me recta via ad Patriam coelestem. Amen.
blocks.english: Lord Jesus Christ, through the sacred wound of Thy right foot, which Thou didst will to imprint upon Thy sincere servant Francis as a sign of special grace: I ask Thee, grant me true and perfect sorrow for my sins and lead me by a straight path to the heavenly homeland. Amen.

blocks.source: Pater noster, et Ave Maria, etc.
blocks.english: Our Father and Hail Mary, etc.
blocks.editorialNote: The printed passage was visually compared with this office’s source pages; its abbreviated form is retained.

blocks.source: Domine Jesu Christe! per sacratum vulnus sinistri pedis, quod sincero tuo servo Francisco in signum singularis gratiae voluisti imprimere: rogo te, custodi et libera me ab omni gravi peccato, omnibusque peccandi occasionibus, ut per gratiam tuam inferni fauces effugere valeam. Amen.
blocks.english: Lord Jesus Christ, through the sacred wound of Thy left foot, which Thou didst will to imprint upon Thy sincere servant Francis as a sign of special grace: I ask Thee, guard and deliver me from every grievous sin and all occasions of sin, that through Thy grace I may escape the jaws of hell. Amen.

blocks.source: Pater noster, et Ave Maria, etc.
blocks.english: Our Father and Hail Mary, etc.
blocks.editorialNote: The printed passage was visually compared with this office’s source pages; its abbreviated form is retained.

blocks.source: Domine Jesu Christe! per vulnus sacratissimi lateris tui, quod sincero tuo servo Francisco in signum singularis gratiae imprimere voluisti: rogo te, concede mihi purum, heroicum, atque Seraphicum erga Deum amorem. Amen.
blocks.english: Lord Jesus Christ, through the wound of Thy most sacred side, which Thou didst will to imprint upon Thy sincere servant Francis as a sign of special grace: I ask Thee, grant me pure, heroic, and seraphic love toward God. Amen.

blocks.source: Pater noster, et Ave Maria, etc.
blocks.english: Our Father and Hail Mary, etc.
blocks.editorialNote: The printed passage was visually compared with this office’s source pages; its abbreviated form is retained.

blocks.source: Omnes hae devotionis possint per quinque dies Veneris addita sacra confessione et communione ante altare, vel saltem imaginem Sancti Patris Francisci peragi, ad obtinendas varias a Deo gratias per intercessionem ejusdem.
blocks.english: [Printed Omnes hae devotionis: unresolved noun agreement] may be performed over five Fridays, with sacramental confession and Communion added, before an altar or at least an image of holy Father Francis, to obtain various graces from God through his intercession.
blocks.editorialNote: 10 October 2026: actual rendered PDF personally compared. The actual devotionis case does not print the expected nominative plural noun; no unprinted ending supplied. Original prepared English/provenance archived; all Latin unchanged.
blocks.originalPreparedEnglish: All these devotions may be performed over five Fridays, with sacramental confession and Communion added, before an altar or at least an image of holy Father Francis, to obtain various graces from God through his intercession [printed agreement irregular].

editorialNotes.text: All printed pages of this office were visually compared. Original Latin, existing English, printed hours and abbreviated conclusions are retained. Prepared English hymn stanzas preserve meaningful line divisions. Defective source readings remain explicitly provisional or unresolved.
